prompt:
This project is CommonJS and we are moving it to ES modules. Convert all of it: the 25 modules under src/ (including src/plugins/), bin/cli.js, run-tests.js and the files in test/ (harness.js and the three *.test.js files).

Rules:
1. Rename every .js file to .mjs (same folder, same base name) and remove the old .js file. Do not add "type": "module" to package.json, and do not add dependencies.
2. Use import and export. Every relative import must include the full file name with the .mjs extension.
3. Export names stay exactly the same as today. A module that sets module.exports to one function or one class becomes a default export. A module that exports an object of names (module.exports = { ... } or exports.name = ...) gets the same names as named exports and no default export. src/index.js exports the objects strings, numbers, arrays, objects and stats and the value VERSION; keep exactly those names.
4. Behavior stays the same, except for two changes that ES modules force. loadPlugin(name) in src/pluginLoader.js loads a plugin with a computed require; make it an async function that returns a promise for the plugin's default export (use a dynamic import). listPlugins() must still return the plugin names without an extension, sorted, so ['reverse', 'upper']. And paths.thisFile() now returns 'paths.mjs', because it reports the module's own file name. __dirname and __filename do not exist in ES modules; Node 24 provides import.meta.dirname and import.meta.filename.
5. src/config.js loads data/defaults.json; keep loading that same file and do not change it.
6. bin/cli.mjs must still run its command line when started with `node bin/cli.mjs sum 1 2 3` and must not run it when another module imports it. It still exports main.
7. The "test" script in package.json must be `node run-tests.mjs`. Running `node run-tests.mjs` must run all 12 existing tests and exit with code 0. Keep all 12 tests.

When you are done, no .js file should remain in the project and no file should use require, module.exports, exports.x = , __dirname or __filename.
